item.title: Shelter In Place Across Mexico Amid Drug Cartel Clash
item.description: Americans in parts of Mexico are being urged to shelter in place following widespread clashes this afternoon among drug cartels. The areas affected include the popular tourist destination of Puerto Vallarta. item.title: Trump Throwing Support Behind TX Republicans
item.description: President Trump is throwing his support behind Texas Governor Greg Abbott. In a Truth Social post on Saturday, Trump endorsed the Republican in his reelection campaign, saying that his is “fighting tirelessly to Champion Texas Values, Grow the Economy, Cut Taxes and Regulations, Support our Amazing Farmers and Ranchers.” The President also showed support for Lt. Governor Dan Patrick, crediting him for helping deliver major primary and general election wins.

item.title: Armed Man Shot And Killed After Entering Secure Perimeter Of Mar-a-Lago, Secret Service Says
item.description: (AP) — An armed man drove into the secure perimeter of Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump’s resort in Palm Beach, Florida, before being shot and killed early Sunday morning, according to a spokesman for the U.S. Secret Service. item.title: Next US-Iran Nuclear Talks Are Thursday In Geneva As Washington Awaits Proposed Deal From Tehran
item.description: (AP) — The United States and Iran will hold their next round of nuclear talks Thursday in Geneva, a facilitator said Sunday, as the Islamic Republic faces both the threat of a U.S. military strike and new protests at home. Oman’s foreign minister, Badr al-Busaidi, confirmed the talks. item.title: At Least 73 People Died In The Attempt To Capture A Mexican Cartel Leader And Its Violent Aftermath
item.description: (AP) — At least 73 people died in Mexico’s attempt to capture the notorious leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the violent aftermath of his death, authorities said Monday as much of the country feared another wave of violence. item.title: Donna Family Sues ICE Over January Immigration Raid
item.description: (Donna, TX) — A Donna family is suing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement over a raid at their home. The lawsuit claims that agents entered the family’s property without a warrant on January 9th. The agents took two noncitizens into custody after allegedly attacking at least two members of the family. The lawsuit claims the ICE agents entered the property without consent, violating their rights under the Fourth and Fifth amendments. A pretrial hearing has been scheduled for May 7th.

item.title: Former Edinburg Fire Chief To Be Added To National Firefighter Memorial
item.description: (Edinburg, TX) — A former Edinburg fire chief will have his name placed on the National Fallen Firefighter Memorial in Maryland. The city has announced that Fire Chief Shawn Snider will be honored during National Fallen Firefighters Memorial Weekend in May. Snider died from cancer in 2023. Current Fire Chief Omar Garza and members of the Snider family will attend the event. Photo provided by City of Edinburg

item.title: Texas May Be Top Data Center Market In The World By 2030
item.description: (Austin, TX) — Research by real estate firm Jones Lang LaSalle indicates Texas could become the world’s top data center market as soon as 2030. Northern Virginia has been the nation’s data center capital for years, providing computing power to the US government in nearby DC, as well as to major companies such as Google. But developers are turning more and more to Texas because of the state’s business-friendly regulatory climate. Tennessee and Ohio are also top emerging data center markets.

item.title: Abbott Faces 10 GOP Challengers, Nine Democrats
item.description: (Austin, TX) — Governor Greg Abbott faces a swarm of challengers as he runs for a fourth term in office. There are ten opponents in the GOP primary, but Abbott has a huge financial advantage and the endorsement of President Donald Trump.
